name: VITEM XI Family Reunion visa

requirement_groups.name: Spouse, child, or dependent of a Brazilian or resident

requirements.blocker_text: Covers spouses/partners, minor children, and dependent parents of a Brazilian citizen or of a foreign national holding valid Brazilian residence.
The sponsoring family member must be a Brazilian citizen or hold valid Brazilian residence status.

evidence_required.document: Marriage certificate, birth certificate, or documentation proving the qualifying family relationship
Sponsor's Brazilian ID or valid residence documentation

outcome.duration_length: tied to the sponsor's status; indefinite if the sponsor is a Brazilian citizen

sources.title: Polícia Federal (gov.br/pf) -- Autorização de Residência, the federal police portal listing residence-authorisation categories including family reunion

notes: citizenship_after_months (12) reflects Lei 13.445/2017 Article 66's reduced naturalisation track for spouses/partners of Brazilian citizens (not legally or factually separated at the time of the grant) -- one of several qualifying conditions that cut the ordinary 4-year residency requirement to 1 year, alongside having a Brazilian child, having rendered relevant service to Brazil, or professional/scientific/artistic distinction (see br_naturalisation for the full Article 66 detail). This is a materially faster spouse-to-citizenship track than most other countries in this dataset, though not as fast as Poland's Karta Polaka-linked routes or Korea's F-6 (both 12 months from a different starting point). pr_after_months uses the same 12-month figure as an approximation, since Brazil's system does not cleanly separate a distinct 'permanent residence' step from naturalisation eligibility the way some other countries in this dataset do -- residência por prazo indeterminado (indefinite-term residence) is the operative status, and naturalisation is a separate, subsequent application on top of it rather than an automatic escalation.
